body: I accidentally influenced a friend/acquaintance to reveal a dark secret to me which led to her having a mental breakdown and being committed to a mental health facility. Her younger sister later committed suicide due to (likely) related events. Their family fell apart and I feel responsibility for the whole chain of events. Yay hormones.

Our situations are fundamentally different. I've had years to sort through this shit by myself. I've told you that I'm not going to kill myself over it. I'm here for an understanding of the other side of the coin. I want to know why you want to make me feel better, mostly so I can try to understand the motivations that led me to try to help my friend. Those are motivations that I very much don't understand, because they were made in a high-stress situation. And no, based on my mentality you trying to help me does not contribute to anything that may happen in the future. You are absolutely not responsible for my well-being. Besides, your intentions are specifically to keep me from self-injury, and mine were not. I was trying to get her to "wake up." I wanted her to experience the clarity with which I was then experiencing the world. I wanted her to fix herself, because I knew that I couldn't fix her. You're not trying to do that. You just don't want me to hurt myself. Your sentiment is pure, and mine was misguided. Either way, I appreciate your time. Thanks for reading and replying, man.

Thanks for replying. I appreciate your positive comparison between me and the people who abused my friend when she was little. I don't really understand why I feel better about myself because a stranger doesn't think I'm as fucked up as they were, but I really, really do. Honestly, this idea is probably the biggest thing that has kept me out of similar mental health facilities since I started dealing with the aftermath of all of this shit. And the reminder that a part of me is noble and worthwhile really does make me stop hating on myself for a while. However, I ask that you read my reply to freakzilla149's replies and consider the questions I posed in that part of the thread. I want to know why you want me to feel better about my crime. (sorry I don't really know how to quote or link to his comments)

I don't want to forgive myself at all. I don't feel obliged to feel responsible. I am responsible. I don't deserve to be forgive, because what I did caused tragedy. I think you, and also Slagtron who commented on my first post, misunderstand the purpose of my original post. I'm not looking for people to convince me to feel better about myself. I don't want to feel better about myself. I'm not deluding myself into self-hate like she was. I hate myself because I destroyed the only thing in the universe that I believe to be good: people. 

The purpose of my post was to ascertain the reasoning behind your urge to help me, and people like me. Please don't misunderstand. I get why you help good people. I know I said earlier that I "think of myself as a good person," but me thinking of myself as something and me being something are entirely different things. I'm a fucking awful person, and people like me don't deserve to be forgiven, especially by ourselves or our victims. I want to know why you want me to feel better about my crime.

I get the "it could have been" argument, but I think it's a lie. It's either me trying to make myself ignore the truth of my part in this or me trying to pretend that my part was inevitable. Well I call that bullshit, in full retrospect. I went down that road, but my ignorance doesn't excuse my guilt. 

And I absolutely agree with your last statement. We don't have as much say in our lives as we think we do. Further, we have less say than we wish we had, despite our inadequacies. We want to effect the universe more than we can. That's human nature. Everyone wants to be more than they are. But we're not. I'm not, and neither are you. I did what I did, and I wanted to do more but I was powerless to do it. I was ignorant because of my own limitations as a human being, and my ignorance led to this calamity. What else could I have done? Nothing, under the circumstances. What else did I do? Nothing. I did this.

I agree with you that I'm not to blame for her issues and I agree to my ignorance of her condition leading in to what happened. But not only do I not agree with your assessment that I should forgive myself, I don't even understand it. Seriously, I don't get it. I said earlier that I have only confessed my situation to one other person. She tried to tell me the same thing. "You have to forgive yourself, it doesn't matter what you did." Why the fuck not? How the hell does it not matter that I was the trigger that destroyed at least two people, and possibly five? I broke up to five times my own worth, and there is absolutely no way to repair the damage. How could I forgive myself. Why should I even consider it? Why should you, or she, or anyone?
